# sophosfirewall_sdwan_route (Data Source)

Looks up an existing SD-WAN route by name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "sophosfirewall_sdwan_route" "example" {
  name = "example"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name of the SD-WAN route. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `applications` (Set of String) Application objects to match. Omit to match any application.
- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `destination_networks` (Attributes) Destination addresses to match. Omit to match any network. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--destination_networks))
- `dscp_marking` (String) DSCP value to mark matching traffic with, as listed by the firewall, e.g. `0-Best Effort`, `46-Expedited Forwarding(EF)` or a plain number such as `5` (0-63).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the route is active. The API reports the status but does not allow changing it.
- `id` (String) UUID of the object assigned by the firewall.
- `inbound_interface` (String) Name of the incoming interface to match. Omit to match any interface.
- `link_selection` (Attributes) How matching traffic leaves the firewall: set either `sdwan_profile` or `primary_gateway` (optionally with `backup_gateway`). Switching between the two forces a new resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--link_selection))
- `position` (String) Where to place the SD-WAN route. One of `top`, `bottom`, `before`, `after`. New rules default to `bottom`. The firewall does not report rule positions, so changes made outside Terraform are not detected.
- `position_reference` (String) Name of the SD-WAN route to place this one `before` or `after`. Required for those positions.
- `service_groups` (Set of String) Service groups to match.
- `services` (Set of String) Services to match. Omit both `services` and `service_groups` to match any service.
- `source_networks` (Attributes) Source addresses to match. Omit to match any network. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source_networks))
- `user_groups` (Set of String) User groups to match.
- `users` (Set of String) Users to match. Omit both `users` and `user_groups` to match any user.

<a id="nestedatt--destination_networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `destination_networks`

Read-Only:

- `countries` (Set of String) Names of countries.
- `country_groups` (Set of String) Names of country groups.
- `fqdn_addresses` (Set of String) Names of FQDN address objects.
- `fqdn_groups` (Set of String) Names of FQDN groups.
- `ipv4_addresses` (Set of String) Names of IPv4 address objects.
- `ipv4_groups` (Set of String) Names of IPv4 address groups.
- `mac_addresses` (Set of String) Names of MAC address objects.


<a id="nestedatt--link_selection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `link_selection`

Read-Only:

- `backup_gateway` (Attributes) Gateway used when the primary gateway is down. Set exactly one of `name` or `wan_link_load_balance`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--link_selection--backup_gateway))
- `primary_gateway` (Attributes) Primary gateway. Set exactly one of `name` or `wan_link_load_balance`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--link_selection--primary_gateway))
- `route_through_specific_gateway` (Boolean) Route only through the selected gateways, dropping traffic when they are unavailable. Defaults to `false`.
- `sdwan_profile` (String) Name of the SD-WAN profile that selects the gateway.

<a id="nestedatt--link_selection--backup_gateway"></a>
### Nested Schema for `link_selection.backup_gateway`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Name of the gateway (a custom gateway or a WAN interface gateway).
- `wan_link_load_balance` (Boolean) Load balance across the configured WAN gateways. Must be `true` when set.


<a id="nestedatt--link_selection--primary_gateway"></a>
### Nested Schema for `link_selection.primary_gateway`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) Name of the gateway (a custom gateway or a WAN interface gateway).
- `wan_link_load_balance` (Boolean) Load balance across the configured WAN gateways. Must be `true` when set.

- `fqdn_groups` (Set of String) Names of FQDN groups.
- `ipv4_addresses` (Set of String) Names of IPv4 address objects.
- `ipv4_groups` (Set of String) Names of IPv4 address groups.
- `mac_addresses` (Set of String) Names of MAC address objects.
